company: Can the company increase prices every year or on every major renewal?
Do customers have few viable alternatives?
Is demand relatively insensitive to price?
Are gross margins maintained or improving during periods of cost inflation?
Does revenue growth come from higher prices rather than just higher volumes?
Can the Chinese replicate and create cheap importable substitutes?
Can inflationary pressures — raw materials, labour wages, interest rates, rental hikes — force margins to shrink?
Are there high switching costs for the customer?
Can a competitor with 100x more resources derail the company's growth trajectory?
Is there high employee attrition or employees that could steal the company's growth secrets and hand them over to competitors?
Does the company enjoy significant mind share or branding advantages?
Can a new technology or some leverage replace the business in the future?
Are there strong lock-in effects including personal ties to the promoters, trophy assets, or some unique advantage which makes the business rock solid?
Does the business enjoy network effects or something that makes customers sticky and even become advocates?
Are the company's offerings significantly better than the nearest competitor's?
Is the market opportunity at least 5-10 times larger than the company's current revenue?
Does the company benefits from a major global macro trend or some global arbitrage?
Is there an unorganized or untapped market that could be captured apart from the above market opportunity?
Does it have a special advantage that kills competition as it grows?
Can the company access required capital easily and cheaply? Can the company expand by adding partners on franchise or transfer the capital risk to the partners?
Can the company access distribution channels easily?
Does scalability come at a steep cost shrinking margins and ROE?
In unexpected circumstances does the company come under severe pressure to return the capital?
Is there some virality or network effect built into the company's offerings?
crypto: Does the asset have credible scarcity mechanics (fixed supply, burn, halving, etc.)?
Do large asset holders have few viable alternatives?
Does the network facilitates genuine economic activity rather than pure speculation?
Do the miners or stakers or validators come under pressure during higher interest rates or increasing energy or hardware costs?
Can Chinese mining pools, validators, or developer teams fork and replicate the network cheaply?
Does the network hold up under coordinated regulatory pressure on exchanges, miners, or stablecoin rails?
Are there high switching costs for holders (wallets, integrations, liquidity positions, L2 commitments)?
Can a competitor with 100x more capital (e.g., a central bank CBDC, a major bank consortium) displace it?
Is developer mindshare and talent concentrated in this ecosystem versus credible alternatives?
Does the project have strong brand recognition in mainstream finance and policy circles?
Can a new technology (quantum computing, alternative L1, zero-knowledge competitor) make this obsolete?
Does the protocol exhibit lock-in via staking, validator sets, liquidity pools, or bridging commitments?
Does it have a genuine network effect where each new user makes existing users' experience better and users even become advocates?
Are the protocol's technical capabilities (throughput, fees, security, composability) significantly better than the nearest credible alternative?
Is the addressable market for the use case 5-10x larger than current on-chain activity?
Are there untapped use cases beyond speculation (payments, DeFi, RWAs, identity, settlement)?
Does it have a special advantage that kills competition as it grows?
Can the project access required liquidity easily through top tier exchanges, hedgefunds and other market makers?
Can it access distribution via major exchanges, wallets, custodians, and fiat on-ramps?
Does scaling come at the cost of decentralization, security, or credible neutrality?
In adverse macro conditions does the project face forced token unlocks or treasury liquidations or collapse of ecosystem?
Is there virality or social momentum built into the network's distribution or culture?
Does the asset benefits from a major global macro trend or some global arbitrage?
